header.running_head: Loving a Muslim for the Pleasure of Allaah

blocks.text: that he had not, Rasulullaah ﷺ told him to do so. He then met Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and said to him, "I like you for the pleasure of Allaah." Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) responded by saying:

"May the One (Allaah) for Whose pleasure you like me, also like you."
When Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) reported back to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Remember that even in mentioning this lies tremendous rewards."[^1]

Hadhrat Mujaahid narrates that when a man passed by him, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) remarked, "That man likes me a lot." "How do you know that, O Ibn Abbaas (RA)?" the people enquired. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) replied, "Because I like him very much."[^2]
Hadhrat Mujaahid also reports that a Sahabi (RA) once held him by his shoulders from the back and said, "You should know that I like you a lot." To this, Hadhrat Mujaahid replied:

"May the One (Allaah) for Whose pleasure you like me, also like you."
The Sahabi (RA) then continued, "Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'When someone likes another person, he should inform him about it.' Had Rasulullaah ﷺ not said this, I would have never informed you." He then proceeded to propose a marriage to Hadhrat Mujaahid saying, "I have a daughter (I wish you would marry. She is blessed with the most excellent qualities but I have to make matters plain to you and (inform you that) She is blind in one eye."[^3]

Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said, "Love for Allaah's pleasure, hate for Allaah's pleasure, make friends for Allaah's pleasure and make enemies for Allaah's pleasure because it is only by this that a person attains Wilaayah (friendship with Allaah). Even though a person may perform salaah in abundance and fast very often, he will never taste true Imaan until he does this. However, (it is sad to note that) bonds between people are now being forged only for worldly motives."[^4]
The Incident of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA)

Hadhrat Auf who was the son of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)'s uterine brother Hadhrat Tufayl reports that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once informed that when she gave away or sold something, (her nephew) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) remarked, "By Allaah! Aa'isha (RA) will have to stop (being so open-handed) or I shall have to restrict her (allowance)." "Did he really say this?"
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.282) has commented on the chain of narrators.
